articles.title: TCU restores Fort Worth Star-Telegram credential that was pulled after reporting on locker room fight resulting in player's dismissal
articles.summary: TCU said it revoked the Star-Telegram's credential due to alleged threats made against the player attacked. Reporter Steven Johnson covered the Horned Frogs'...
articles.body:
The TCU football program has restored credentials for the Fort Worth Star-Telegram after the newspaper's access was revoked for its coverage of a locker room altercation that resulted in safety Jacob Fields being dismissed from the team .

"Today, TCU Athletics fully restored media credentials to the Fort Worth Star-Telegram," a statement issued by TCU said . "In a series of productive discussions, we made clear our position and resolved to move forward. We respect their role as an independent news source and voice in our community, and we look forward to the season ahead."

"Today, TCU Athletics fully restored media credentials to the Fort Worth Star-Telegram," a statement issued by TCU said .

"In a series of productive discussions, we made clear our position and resolved to move forward. We respect their role as an independent news source and voice in our community, and we look forward to the season ahead."

Star-Telegram reporter Steven Johnson reported on Aug. 18 that tensions had been developing in the locker room, but coaches made no attempts to de-escalate the situation despite being informed of what was happening. Head coach Sonny Dykes reportedly did not realize how serious the issues were among players.

After the Star-Telegram reported that its credentials had been pulled , a TCU athletic department spokesman said the decision was made because of alleged threats made to sophomore receiver Dozie Ezukanma, who had been punched by Fields. The newspaper's report of the incident did not identify Ezukanma until the player revealed he was the one attacked on a social media video.

Johnson traveled to Dublin, Ireland, to cover TCU's 15-10 loss to North Carolina in its season opener, but did so from the stands rather than the press box at Aviva Stadium.

Jacob Fields dismissed from team after locker room fight

Fields was dismissed from the team earlier this month after the locker room fight. The incident in question occurred Aug. 13.

Ezukanma alleged in an Instagram video that Fields "sucker punched" him, causing his head to hit the floor and knocking him unconscious. He said Fields also kicked him in the head, the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reported .

A TCU football staffer reported the incident to campus police the next day, according to an official report . Fields was subsequently dismissed from the team and a warrant for Fields' arrest stated that Ezukanma suffered a brain bleed from the attack.

Fields was arrested on Aug. 30 after turning himself in to Tarrant County police on a charge of aggravated assault causing serious bodily injury. The senior transfer was booked into the Tarrant County Jail and was released later that day after posting a $50,000 bond .

articles.title: Ipswich Town v Liverpool: How the players rated
articles.summary: How Liverpool and Ipswich Town's players rated following their Premier League match.
articles.body:
Alexander Isak's two early goals set Liverpool on the way to their first Premier League win of the season - and a first for new manager Andoni Iraola - at Ipswich Town .

Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below.

Isak double earns Iraola first Liverpool win

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Kjell Scherpen: Desperately poor for Alexander Isak's early goal. Weak and meant Ipswich got off to the worst possible start. A couple of decent saves but the damage was done. 4

Dara O'Shea: Led from the front as always but Ipswich's defence struggled against the movement of Isak and the creation of Gakpo. He had a hard time. 5

Issa Diop: Towering figure always willing to indulge in the physical changes but this was a tough night after those two early Liverpool goals. 6

Jacob Greaves: Stern test against the inspired Cody Gakpo, showing the quality he will face in the Premier League. 5

Leif Davis: Tested defensively but was always competitive. Lent weight to attacks and had a chance with a far post header. 6

Sasa Lukic: Will bring experience to Ipswich Town but on this night Liverpool 's midfield was too powerful. 5

Exequiel Palacios: Tried to bring some composure to Ipswich Town 's game but was fighting a losing battle. 6

Abdul Fatawu: Pace but little end product. Energetic but erratic. 5

Julio Enciso: Ipswich's main threat. Tireless. Might have done more with the final ball but never gave up even when odds were against him. 7

Daizen Maeda: Anonymous. Made no impact at all and no surprise when taken off. 5

Emersonn: Battled hard but no luck against Van Dijk and Jacquet. 5

Jack Clarke (on 66 Maeda): Introduced when the game was lost. 5

Zian Flemming (on 66, Emersonn): Couple of bustling contributions. 5

Subs not used: Walton, Furlong, Kipre, Florentino, Nunez

Alisson: Lucky to get away with misjudging a first-half corner. The occasional anxious moment but no harm done. 6

Ronald Araujo: Strong in the air and on the ground on an impressive Premier League debut at right-back. Important interventions by being in the right place at the right time. 7

Virgil van Dijk: Usual unruffled self in the face of some frantic Ipswich Town attacking. 7

Jeremy Jacquet: Solid alongside Van Dijk. Continues to look a very fine acquisition. 6

Milos Kerkez: Occasionally troubled by Fatawu's pace but never in huge difficulties. 6

Dominik Szoboszlai : Driving runs from midfield and always willing to test the keeper. Iraola should never use him at right-back. 7

Alexis Mac Allister: Still not quite at his best. Too many misplaced passes but never hides or shirks responsibility. 6

Florian Wirtz: Busy but occasionally lightweight. As so often, showed subtle touches that hint at good things to come. 6

Alexander Isak: The best of Alexander Isak at last. Running behind a defence with pace and clever movement with cool finishes. Finally showed why Liverpool bought him. 8

Victor Munoz: Willing and pacy out wide but could have delivered more end product. 6

Cody Gakpo: Could have been playing for Manchester City . How glad Liverpool are he wasn't. Two superb passes for Isak's opening goals, Truly outstanding performance. 9

Bradley Barcola (on 64, Munoz): Showed one or two flashes of the lightning pace the £123m signing will bring to Liverpool . 5

Ryan Gravenberch (on 64, Isak): Brought on to shut down any potential Ipswich Town revival.

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Frimpong, Tsimikas, Endo, Ngumoha

After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.

articles.title: Football gossip: Bissouma, Wharton, Baena, Mane, Richarlison, Castellanos
articles.summary: Chelsea were offered ex-Tottenham midfielder Yves Bissouma, Manchester City and Chelsea showed interest in Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton, Arsenal are considering move for Barcelona's Raphinha, plus more.
articles.body:
Chelsea were offered ex- Tottenham midfielder Yves Bissouma, Manchester City and Chelsea showed interest in Crystal Palace 's Adam Wharton, and Arsenal considering move for Barcelona's Raphinha.

Chelsea were offered former Mali midfielder Yves Bissouma, 30, who left Tottenham in the summer, as a replacement for Argentina's Enzo Fernandez, 25, who joined Manchester City for £125m. (Sun) , external

Manchester City and Chelsea are believed to be among those who showed an interest in signing England midfielder Adam Wharton, 22, before the transfer deadline, with Crystal Palace rejecting all bids. (Guardian) , external

Aston Villa , Manchester City and Newcastle United are showing interest in Spain winger Alex Baena but Atletico Madrid have no plans to sell the 25-year-old. (CaughtOffside) , external

Wolves could have sold Portugal Under-21s forward Mateus Mane before the transfer window closed, with Liverpool and Manchester United both admirers of the 18-year-old. (Teamtalk) , external

Arsenal are considering a £68m offer for Barcelona and Brazil winger Raphinha, 29, in January. (Fichajes - in Spanish) , external

Tottenham are considering paying up Richarlison's contract to allow the out-of-favour 29-year-old Brazil forward to leave the club on a free transfer. (Talksport) , external

Everton made a verbal offer of £40m plus £5m in add-ons to West Ham for Argentine striker Taty Castellanos on transfer deadline day but the move came too late for the Hammers to sanction the 27-year-old's exit. (Teamtalk) , external

Newcastle United manager Matthias Jaissle's desire to keep English attacking midfielder Jacob Murphy meant the Tyneside club rejected two offers for the 31-year-old from Nottingham Forest . (Football Insider) , external

articles.title: David Beckham, Wayne Rooney and Newport's Harrison Biggins: The long-shot kings
articles.summary: After Harrison Biggins' 70-yard goal, BBC Sport Wales recalls some of the best long-range strikes over the years.
articles.body:
David Beckham and Wayne Rooney are famous for their long-range goals, but Newport County's Harrison Biggins has eclipsed even their best efforts.

Biggins' screamer in Newport's 2-1 defeat at Salford City has been measured at exactly 77.7 yards, which may well be an English Football League (EFL) record.

The sensational effort might even put Beckham's 59-yard stunner for Manchester United at Wimbledon in 1997 in the shade.

It also surpasses in distance Rooney's remarkable 61-yard goal for Everton at West Ham United in 2017.

Fans of League Two Newport are no strangers to applauding long-range 'worldie' goals.

Their former goalkeeper Tom King proudly boasts the Guinness World Record distance for a goal scored in a competitive football match - an astonishing 105-yard effort for Newport at Cheltenham in 2021.

BBC Sport Wales takes a look back at some of the furthest goals ever scored.

Where else could this list start, but with the World Record holder Tom King.

When Newport faced Cheltenham in blustery conditions at the Jonny-Rock Stadium in 2021, even King himself could have not expected what would follow.

The now-Everton stopper prepared to take an ordinary goal-kick.

But aided by the wind, his strike travelled the length of the pitch, bouncing over Cheltenham goalkeeper Joshua Griffiths and into the net.

It was the first time a goalkeeper had scored in a match in the English Football League since Barry Roche for Morecambe against Portsmouth in 2016.

King later admitted that even he didn't know how to celebrate the moment as he surpassed Asmir Begovic's previous record of 100.5 yards.

Moritz Stoppelkamp, SC Paderborn (91 yards)

If King owns the overall record, then Moritz Stoppelkamp's effort for Paderborn is the longest ever scored by an outfield player.

Paderborn were leading Hannover 1-0 in a Bundesliga match in September 2014 when the visitors committed everyone forward in search of a late equaliser, including goalkeeper Ron-Robert Zieler.

After the danger was cleared, the ball dropped to Stoppelkamp on the edge of his own penalty area.

With one touch to set himself, he unleashed a stunning strike on the volley from 83 metres (91 yards), into the unguarded net.

The effort set a new Bundesliga distance record, surpassing Giorgos Tzavellas' previous mark by 10 metres - more than 13 yards further than Biggins' strike.

Harrison Biggins, Newport County (77.7 yards)

Biggins' effort may not have threatened King's world record or be the furthest scored by an outfielder, but it has already secured a place among the EFL's most memorable long-range goals.

Newport County were under pressure against Salford City when the midfielder collected possession deep inside his own half.

Rather than simply clearing his lines or threading Shaquille Gwengwe in on goal, Biggins took a touch, beat a man and, spotting Norris well off his line, unleashed a rocket.

His stunning effort sailed over the stranded Norris and nestled in the net, prompting jubilant celebrations from the travelling supporters.

Unfortunately for Newport , the goal ultimately came in a 2-1 defeat after Salford staged a late comeback.

But it was further evidence of a player who has never been afraid to attempt the ambitious.

Newport boss Hayden Mullins has seen the midfielder attempt that kind of spectacular effort three times, the first a near-halfway lob against Roma in pre-season and the second striking the post from a 40-yard volley against Bristol Rovers.

"The goalkeeper was pretty high out the box and if there's one person who's going to try that, it is him," said Mullins.

"I didn't expect him to score, but it is a fantastic goal."

Salford rally late to sink Newport for first league win

Fleetwood into top half with win at 10-man Newport

Breaking down Chelsea's staggering 39 summer exits

Biggins' strike stands at almost 20-yards further out than Rooney's tremendous strike at Goodison Park.

But what made Rooney's that little more special was that it clinched the former England striker's first hat-trick in more than six years.

As Joe Hart dispossessed the onrushing Dominic Calvert-Lewin, he could do little to prevent the ball falling to Manchester United's all-time record goalscorer.

And when it fell at Rooney's feet, he made no mistake in drilling the ball over everyone and into the net.

A fine strike for a man who scored 366 career goals, but few more memorable than this.

Though not known for his goalscoring ability, netting just 16 times during his five-year spell at Liverpool, Xabi Alonso always had an eye for the spectacular long-range attempt.

Even he admits that his brilliant strike at St James' Park to give the Reds a 2-0 victory against Newcastle United is the best of his career.

The ball broke to the current Chelsea boss just inside his own half and having seen keeper Steve Harper off his line, his audacious effort from just over 60 yards nestled in the back of the net.

Harper in his scramble to get back slipped and could only watch in wonder as the ball sailed over his head.

It was the second time in a year that Alonso had scored from inside his own half, having found the net against Luton in the FA Cup in January that same year – so Newcastle cannot say they were not warned.

Josh Windass, Sheffield Wednesday (around 60 yards)

Current Wrexham man Josh Windass has always had the ability to shoot from range.

But none of his goals compare to the 60-yard strike he hit on New Year's Day, which ensured 2025 opened with a bang for Sheffield Wednesday supporters.

Running on to a loose ball inside his own half, the Owls forward took one touch before spotting goalkeeper Jacob Zetterstrom off his line and sending a remarkable effort looping into the far corner.

It sparked memorable celebrations at Hillsborough, but not from Windass, who instead soaked up the applause in his usual nonchalant demeanour , allowing himself just one wry smile.

David Beckham, Manchester United (57 yards)

No list of long-range goals would be complete without this man's name.

The goal that propelled Beckham into the headlines was one of the most impressive the Premier League era has seen.

The opening day of the season. Selhurst Park, 57 yards out, last minute. A ball broke to Beckham who - as has been a common theme throughout these goals - spotted goalkeeper Neil Sullivan off his line, went for the spectacular.

His inch-perfect attempt lobbed Sullivan and, in a career in which the former England captain scored 127 goals, this 57-yard lob against AFC Wimbledon perhaps ranks as his greatest strike.

Biggins' effort, scored during a wet and windy Tuesday night League Two encounter, will not attract the acclaim of the renowned goals from Beckham, Alonso or Rooney.

But the former Shrewsbury Town man may well have written himself in the EFL history books with his phenomenal 77.7-yard strike.

articles.title: Doblete tempranero de Isak da la victoria al Liverpool
articles.standfirst: Alexander Isak firma un doblete para anotar la primera victoria de la temporada del Liverpool
articles.summary: Alexander Isak firma un doblete para anotar la primera victoria de la temporada del Liverpool
articles.body: Nueve minutos tardó el Liverpool en firmar la victoria pues el temprano doblete de Isak puso por delante a los Reds frente a un Ipswich sin opciones. Andoni Iraola apostaba por los titulares del último partido frente al Nottingham Forrest a excepción de la titularidad de Ronald Araujo. En el banquillo de al lado, Gary O'Neil presentaba igualmente un único cambio en el once inicial frente a la derrota de Old Trafford. Los Reds buscaban su primera victoria esta temporada y se ponían el mono de trabajo para conseguirlo. Los goles no tardaban en llegar. Un doblete de Isak en apenas nueve minutos ponía el resultado a favor de los rojos. Generando peligro y cogiendo el ritmo de juego que le ha faltado al Liverpool en las dos jornadas previas, es como insistía el conjunto de Anfield para mantener la ventaja hasta el descanso. Los segundos 45 minutos se presentaban de la misma manera. Mucho dominio Red y disparos desafortunados de los Blues. Enciso disparaba en múltiples ocasiones pero Alisson no se equivocaba. El Liverpool seguía jugando a lo suyo, llegar al área y amenazar la portería local. Dos disparos de Szoboszlai obligaban a Scherpen a sacar los puños. El guardameta de O'Neil evitaba la goleada. Los cambios llegaban y el debut de Bradley Barcola con él. La banda izquierda era su pista pero el centro hacia Gakpo no encontraba la red. El Ipswich perdía posesión muy rápido y aunque Clarke intentó un disparo, este golpeó en su compañero Diop y ni rozó los tres palos. Un posible penalti podría haber supuesto el tercero para los de Iraola pero el fuera de juego previo a la falta sobre Szoboszlai cambiaba la dirección de la jugada. Fueron cinco de añadido, pero ni eso fue suficiente para cambiar el pronóstico que se preveía desde los primeros minutos. El Liverpool consigue anotar los tres puntos en Portman Road ante un Ipswich con pocas amenazas que llegasen al área Red. El siguiente enfrentamiento liguero para los de Anfield será en casa ante el Fullham de Arbeloa.

articles.title: World Cup review: FA to canvass England players in analysing tournament
articles.summary: The Football Association's review into England's World Cup campaign will canvass the opinions of players involved in the tournament.
articles.body:
The Football Association's review into England's World Cup campaign will canvass the opinions of players involved in the tournament.

English football's governing body has started the post-tournament review they conduct after every major international competition. The FA says the review is the standard process it undertakes after all tournaments.

Head coach Thomas Tuchel and members of his backroom team were at St George's Park last week where they were involved in unpacking their performance in north America with a wider report into the team's World Cup campaign to be delivered at a later date.

And it is understood members of Tuchel's squad will be spoken to, and their feedback taken into account, as part of the review process.

The players' involvement in the review provides an interesting dynamic given the emerging sense from members of the World Cup squad that Tuchel's substitutions and tactical approach contributed to their semi-final loss to Argentina - despite taking a 1-0 lead through Anthony Gordon.

BBC Sport revealed in the 24 hours after that defeat that at least three senior players privately expressed misgivings about Tuchel's approach in the closing stages of the game.

There was a widely held view that Tuchel's changes and tactical set-up were too defensive late on as they conceded two late goals to lose 2-1.

The ongoing review will also look into the impact of the team's permanent Kansas City base during the tournament.

After every game, they returned to Kansas City - and the effects of the travelling will be analysed.

England went on to defeat France in the bronze medal match to record their best World Cup finish since lifting the trophy in 1966.

With that in mind, key figures at the FA view the tournament as a success and the organisation has backed Tuchel before the Euro 2028 qualifying campaign.

England will play their first game since the World Cup in the Nations League against Spain on 26 September. They will also face two matches in the tournament against the Czech Republic, either side of playing Croatia, during the next international window.

articles.title: El Madrid no puede perder este partido
articles.standfirst: La opinión de José Vicente Hernáez
articles.summary: La opinión de José Vicente Hernáez
articles.body: Así es. Primera derrota del Real Madrid. Primera derrota de José Mourinho. Fatal. Una derrota que no entraba en los pronósticos, aunque el Madrid no le había ganado al Betis en su casa en las cuatro últimas temporadas. Pero, las cosas como son, lo diga Agamenón o su porquero, el Madrid no puede perder este partido. Lo tenía que haber ganado por lo civil o por lo criminal (mejor lo primero, claro), como sucedió con el Espanyol. Se deja tres puntos importantes que le va a costar mucho recuperar. ¿Y por qué no ganó el Madrid este partido? En primer lugar, no mereció perderlo, aunque el empate tampoco habría evitado este mal sabor porque a día de hoy un empate es casi una derrota. Y no lo ganó el Madrid por varias circunstancias. Una: un segundo tiempo malo de verdad, con mucho control pero sin ideas arriba. Dos: Mbappé fue decisivo...para mal. En el primer tiempo falló la ocasión más clara de todo el partido ¡por dos veces! Y en el minuto 93 falló un penalti que no debió haber fallado. Para eso él es el gran especialista. Tres: Alvaro Valles, portero del Betis, fue el héroe del partido, no sólo por el penalti parado (los penaltis se fallan, no se paran, como decía el gran Puskas) sino por varias jugadas más, entre otras una en el primer tiempo en la que evitó el 0-1 de Huijsen (tras un pase, cómo no, de Arda Güler). Cuatro: Bellingham no apareció...cuando parecía por sus últimos encuentros que estaba en un gran momento de forma. Cinco: Vinícius no se fue de nadie. Provocó el penalti, es cierto, pero está muy lejos de ser el Vinicius al que se le ha dado el Himalaya por renovar su contrato. Seis: la marcha de Arda Güler, seguramente por tener una tarjeta amarilla y para evitar que el equipo se quedase con diez en la segunda mitad. Lo que ocurre es que al irse Güler se fue también el Madrid. Mourinho tiene claro qué cambios tiene que hacer y cuáles no hacer. En fin, una derrota que duele. Y duele porque no se veía venir. El Madrid de Mourinho ha dejado de ilusionar de golpe. Y el martes le espera el Inter. Una prueba de fuego

images.caption: Mourinho, durante el partido ante el Betis. EFE

articles.title: Hamburger SV vs. 1. FSV Mainz 05 preview: Both teams look for first goal and win
articles.summary: Hamburg entertain Mainz in the penultimate matchday 2 game of the Bundesliga as the two teams are yet to register their first goal of the campaign.Hamburger...
articles.body:
Hamburg entertain Mainz in the penultimate matchday 2 game of the Bundesliga as the two teams are yet to register their first goal of the campaign.

HSV bosses were busy closing deals on deadline day after HSV's poor showing in the first Topspiel of the season. Merlin Polzin's side were thoroughly dominated by Borussia Dortmund despite the respectable 2-0 scoreline.

However, the excitement is palpable ahead of the first home game of the season after they signed three players in the final hours of the transfer window. Fábio Vieira signed on a permanent deal after his impressive season on loan, while Zakaria El Ouahdi and David Møller Wolfe arrived at Volksparkstadion to fill the gaps in fullback positions.

HSV's latest signings are all candidates to improve last week's lineup. However, Louis Lemke will hope to make his full debut at Volksparkstadion weeks after becoming the first 16-year-old to score for the club.

On the contrary, Mainz did their business early in the market. The 05ers even allowed Andreas Hanche-Olsen and Marco Richter to depart late without signing replacements. The former joined Robert Lewandowski at Chicago Fire, while Richter is now a free agent after they agreed on a contract termination.

Urs Fischer's side looked to be a bit weak in squad depth compared to last season, but there will be no European nights this time around. The experienced coach started the campaign with a goalless draw with newly-promoted Paderborn last week.

Dominik Kohr, who suffered a late injury against Paderborn minutes after coming close to breaking the deadlock, is out of the game. Eric Martel has to wait longer for his Mainz debut, but Stefan Posch is now ready for the starting lineup.

HSV recorded their biggest victory back in Bundesliga in this fixture last term. Rayan Philippe, who has now joined Paderborn on loan, scored twice in a 4-0 victory against Bo Svensson's men. With Fischer in charge of Mainz in the return fixture, star figures Nadiem Amiri and Fábio Vieira were on target as the sides shared the spoils at Mewa Arena.

articles.title: Ohio State vs. Ball State Buckeyes Wire staff predictions for Week 1
articles.summary: It's Week 1 of the college football season and Ohio State kicks it off against Ball State. Our Buckeyes Wire staff predicts the score, and why.
articles.body:
There's no better time of the year in Columbus, Ohio, than college football season, and after a long wait and a loss by Ohio State to Miami (FL) in the College Football Playoff , the Buckeyes are ready to get back on the field when they host Ball State at 12:30 p.m. ET on Saturday in the 'Shoe.

The oddsmakers -- heck, almost anyone without a Ball State degree (and even most with one) believe this one will be over shortly after scarlet and gray colors step off the bus. The Cardinals are traveling from Indiana to take on the preseason No. 1 team , and there is talent oozing out of all corners of the Ohio State roster.

But the game must be played, and so we'll keep an eye on several things as we get to see this year's Buckeye squad for the first time in 2026. For years now, we like to have our Buckeyes Wire writers take turns predicting the score of each OSU game with a little synopsis of what things will look like, so here we go with Week 1.

Ohio State hasn't lost a season-opening game since it lost to Miami (FL) back in 1999. Consider that streak very safe against a Ball State team that is coming off of a very rough year and just doesn't have the athletes and depth to compete with the talent the Buckeyes have.

There might be a little rust for OSU, but the players and coaches will shake it off early enough and score in bunches on the way to a blowout win. It'll be a great time to get some depth pieces in the game and rest the starters for what's coming next week against Texas .

Score Prediction: Ohio State 52, Ball State 7

The Buckeyes get a tune-up game before heading to Austin. Never overlook an opponent, but Ball State is one of the bottom dwellers of the Mid-American Conference. The forecast is calling for rain, which may be the only thing that can slow down the OSU offensive attack. Unfortunately for the Cardinals, a little weather won't be enough as the Buckeyes roll.

Score Prediction: Ohio State 42, Ball State 3

Ohio State enters the game on Saturday with sky-high expectations once again as the No. 1 team in the country. Ryan Day may want the Buckeyes to get to a strong and early lead so they can let their younger players get snaps in preparation for the top-5 showdown the following week in Austin.

Score Prediction: Ohio State 49, Ball State 3

It's the start of a new season, and there's a lot of optimism around what this Ohio State team can be. Julian Sayin and Jeremiah Smith are the obvious storylines, but this could arguably be one of OSU's most talented rosters top to bottom in the last few years. There are a lot of young and promising stars who will look to build on successful early-season performances. Because of that, and the fact that it's Senior Day, I expect nothing short of a terrific outing from the Buckeyes. Things may take a bit longer to click offensively with new OC Arthur Smith , but the excitement level is there. Slow start into a dominant overall performance. Ohio State rolls.

Score Prediction: Ohio State 56, Ball State 6

articles.title: ‘Exceptional’ Xavi Espart tipped to stay in Barcelona first team by ex-La Masia chief
articles.summary: Some strong backing from a man who knows the youngster well.
articles.body:
Xavi Espart has been making waves at Barcelona this season after starring for Hansi Flick's side in the first three games of the new La Liga campaign.

The 19-year-old has already played his way into the first-team squad for the 2026-27 season and been handed the No. 12 shirt. He's also now being tipped to stay in the starting XI.

Former La Masia director Jordi Roura says that Espart is still learning the full-back position but will simply get even better as he continues his development.

"He'll be able to do it. At his age, the room for improvement is enormous," says Jordi Roura. "He has the level to establish himself in the first team and have consistent playing time," he told AS.

"He's much stronger than he looks. He has a very powerful lower body and is holding his own well during sprints, anticipating plays well."

Roura also spoke about when he first brought Espart to the club

"When I signed him, we were always struck by how well he played football," he added. "He's been characterized as a very technical player, who reads and understands the game very well."

Espart shone yet again last time out against Rayo. Roura hailed his performance as "exceptional" and said the youngster "gave a real masterclass."

The teenager will now be hoping to get the nod again on Sunday against Valencia in La Liga.

articles.title: 49ers got a 16-hour flight to Australia. Here's how my journey compared
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers got a direct flight to Melbourne from SFO with lay-flat seats. For a new reporter flying coach, connecting through New Zealand, it wa...
articles.body:
Before their season opener across the globe on Thursday, the San Francisco 49ers flew to Melbourne, Australia, a week before kickoff. The team departed San Francisco late Wednesday night and arrived in Australia early Friday morning (local time) in an effort to adjust their body clocks well ahead of game day.

While the 17-hour time difference between California and Melbourne after a 16-hour flight sounds daunting, was the experience actually that bad? Here's what we learned, and here's how my travel experience compared to that of the 49ers.

The 49ers were chartered on a nonstop, 16-hour United Airlines flight from San Francisco International Airport to Melbourne. Players, coaches and executives were treated to luxury lay-flat seats where they could stretch their legs, rest their heads on a pillow and enjoy a semi-legitimate sleeping experience.

That sounds nice. Although maybe not nice enough to meet the standards of certain players. Offensive tackle Trent Williams said Wednesday morning in Santa Clara, hours ahead of the 49ers' flight, that the standard lay-flat seats for players on road trips are not that comfortable for anyone over 6-foot-1.

"Hopefully we get something a little bit bigger than that," Williams said, "or it's gonna be torture."

It appears some 49ers got adequate rest. In an interview with local Australian TV station 10 Sport, offensive lineman Enrique Cruz Jr. (6-foot-5, 313 pounds) and defensive tackle Gracen Halton (6-foot-3, 293 pounds) said they slept 11 hours and "the whole time," respectively.

Kicker Eddy Piñeiro , on the other hand, said on the Australian Football League broadcast that he remained "a little jet-lagged" Friday night after sleeping just a couple hours on the flight.

I dare Williams - or any other Niner, for that matter - to attempt my flying experience. I flew economy on Air New Zealand with a layover in Auckland. On my first flight - a 12-hour trip from SFO to Auckland before another four-hour flight to Melbourne - I slept four hours. I couldn't recline my seat more than two inches. The $15 memory foam neck pillow I bought in the international terminal's convenience store offered some pillow-like characteristics, but my head remained upright the whole night.

The saving grace was that the middle seat in my row remained vacant. My aisle seat suddenly had a decent amount of legroom, and I used it to my advantage, stretching my legs into the open space under the middle seat. The window seat passenger in my row smartly pushed down the armrest and used most of the middle seat as her personal foot rest.

On the first flight, we received two hot meals: one "dinner" early in-flight and one "breakfast" as our 6 a.m. Auckland arrival approached. In case I hadn't eaten enough breakfast, I got another one on my second flight to Melbourne, since that one took off around 9 a.m. local time.

After landing Friday morning, our next big challenge was beating the jet lag. The 49ers seemed to do it better than I did. The team had a training session and a few welcome events the afternoon of their first day (Friday). At night, San Francisco players attended an Australian Football League match between the Geelong Cats and Carlton Football Club at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, the 100,000-capacity stadium in which next week's game between the 49ers and Rams will be played.

Good on them for putting in a full day's work in the new time zone. After checking into my hotel and exploring the Southbank Riverwalk in downtown Melbourne in the late afternoon, I passed out at 8 p.m., not long after sunset.

Safe to say - as I write this story wide awake at 5 a.m. Saturday in Melbourne - jet lag is no joke. Although it was a challenging travel experience, one thing is certain: The 49ers will be well-adjusted by game time.

The Los Angeles Rams , on the other hand? They're expected to arrive about 24 hours before kickoff. Best of luck to them.
